Subject: Dedicated capacity — proposal and options

Hi Maya,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is a concise proposal with three reservation paths we discussed. High-level summary below so your procurement and engineering teams can review quickly:

• Option A — Compact starter cluster
  - Cluster size: 8 x A100 (shared lane)
  - Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 8
  - Typical sustained throughput: supports low-volume production; warm-up credits included
  - Ramp: ready immediately, scale to 2x in month 3

• Option B — Production baseline (recommended for initial ML workloads)
  - Cluster size: 32 x A100 (dedicated pool)
  - Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 16 (floor to preserve latency SLOs)
  - Ramp: 40% baseline month 1 → 70% month 2 → 100% month 4
• Option C — Performance-forward (burst and throughput)
  - Cluster size: 64 x A100 + burst pool
  - Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 32
  - Ramp: staged activation over 3 months, with burst credits for traffic spikes

Key operational notes:
- We recommend enabling KV-prefix caching and a 2–4s batching window for inference pipelines that tolerate micro-batching; this cuts token cost without increasing tail latency for typical request mixes.
- We can carve a hot-lane for low-latency models (single-GPU serving) and a throughput lane for batched workloads.
- Pricing and term options are in the attached PDF; there’s a standard 12-month commitment and a 3-month trial credit alternative if you prefer a gentler ramp.

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Proposal_Novatrix_20261031.pdf (proposal deck)

Can you share procurement timelines and whether a 3-month staged activation (we highlighted in Option C) maps to your go-to-prod date? Happy to hop on a short call to walk the deck.

Best,

Maya — quick technical notes to answer #1 and #2:

• Latency guidance: For low-batch (<=4) Llama/decoder-style models, a baseline of 8 GPUs (A100/80GB) with a hot-lane allocation (1 GPU pinned) can meet ~200–250ms p95 for shorter contexts (<=512 tokens). If you expect concurrent model combos (NER + summarize in series) we recommend moving to 16–32 GPUs to keep p95 headroom.

• Burst activation: Burst pools are pre-provisioned capacity; activation is immediate (seconds) but sustained burst depends on available pool credits and regional capacity. We can reserve a warm-standby set for guaranteed bursts (additional cost) or provide soft burst guarantees with automatic fallback to a compatible smaller model.

• Warmup & prefix caching: Adding a 10–20 minute pre-warm window for high-traffic hours reduces cold-KV misses and dramatically lowers early-run latency.

I attached a short capacity workbook with scenario knobs — estimated concurrency per model and token burn for the three options.

Attachment: Novatrix_capacity_estimates_20261101.xlsx (workbook)

Happy to jump on a short technical call if you want us to walk the numbers.

— Priyom
